taskPacket.objective: The worker/judge independence rule compares the canonical provider (openai, anthropic, zhipu, deepseek, google) derived from a runtime's harness, model and route, never the free-text vendor label, and a declared vendor that contradicts the derived provider is refused (first half of R18).
instructions: New module src/contract/provider.mjs exporting canonicalProvider(runtime) and nothing that duplicates an existing export. Derivation, in order: (1) the route a runtime declares to another provider: codex config.model_provider (for example deepseek) and dsh config.provider (deepseek-official is deepseek); (2) the model id's family: claude-*, opus, sonnet, fable, haiku are anthropic; gpt-* and o<digit>* are openai; gemini-* is google; glm-* is zhipu; deepseek-* is deepseek (agy resells claude and gpt-oss models, so an agy runtime serving claude-sonnet-4-6 is anthropic); (3) the harness default already in src/harnesses/index.mjs DEFAULT_HARNESS_VENDORS (claude anthropic, codex openai, agy google, zcode zhipu). The test harnesses replay and exec-jsonl have no canonical provider: for them the declared vendor stands, as today.

validateRuntime (src/contract/runtime.mjs) refuses a runtime whose declared vendor contradicts its derived provider, naming both (for example `runtime sol declares vendor openai-sol but codex gpt-5.6-sol is provider openai`); a declared vendor equal to the derived provider is accepted, and the validated runtime's vendor becomes the derived provider.

Switch every worker-against-judge comparison to the canonical provider. The sites, measured 2026-09-24: src/contract/index.mjs validateContract near :293-324 (worker, judge, worker fallback chain); src/engine/lifecycle.mjs handleProviderExhaustion near :677-701 (judge_fallback_vendor_conflict; lifecycle.mjs has 7 lines left, so read the provider through a helper it already imports or move code out, never past 800); src/engine/failover.mjs admitsAffinity near :219-227; src/engine/runtime-discovery.mjs composeAssignments, nextSameTierRuntime, strongest; src/plan/routing.mjs forbiddenJudgeVendors; src/plan/preflight.mjs refuseUnplannableRuntimes; src/harnesses/catalogue.mjs suggestedAllocation; src/cli/setup.mjs keptJudgeDefault, defaultJudge, crossVendor; src/host/preflight.mjs reachableRuntimes stand-in judge. If validateRuntime already stamps the derived provider on vendor, a site that reads the validated vendor is already right: say which sites needed no change.

Tests that paired two runtimes of one provider with distinct labels now fail by design. Fix them without weakening what they assert: in test/helpers.mjs keep the fixture judge id `sol` but make it a runtime of another provider that the fake codex binary still serves, for example `sol: { harness: "codex", model: "deepseek-v4-flash", config: { model_provider: "deepseek", "model_providers.deepseek.env_key": "DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" } }`, and update the comment. Then fix every other test the suite shows failing on the label (measured sites: test/campaign/launch-failed, unpark, metrics, chain, chain-refresh; test/engine/routing, read-only-judge, failover, review, tier-exhaustion, scope-usage, worker-result, runtime-discovery; test/plan/template, the planner vendors distinct test), each to a pair of distinct derived providers, keeping each test's intent.

skills/faberun/references/contract.md shows free-text vendors (openai-sol, zhipu-flash): make its examples declare no vendor or the derived one and say in one sentence that the rule compares the provider derived from harness, model and route. The skill byte budget must not grow; test/contract/runtime.test.mjs guards that file.

Pin the test 'the vendor rule compares the provider derived from harness and model' in the new file test/contract/provider.test.mjs: the derivation table (route, model family, harness default, replay keeps its label), the refusal of a contradicting label, and validateContract refusing a codex gpt worker judged by a codex gpt runtime labelled differently.

taskPacket.objective: A plan's verification proof.ref may be the command's index or the exact text of one of the node's verification commands; freezing normalizes text to the index (R21).
instructions: src/contract/definition-of-done.mjs validateVerificationRef (near :111) accepts only an index today and throws `.ref must be the zero-based index of a verification command`. Accept, when the node's verification commands are known, a string equal to one command's argv joined by single spaces (the form the planner's models wrote, measured in choose-the-judges R5), and resolve it to that command's index. A text that matches no command is refused with the node id and the commands that exist, one per line.

src/plan/template.mjs validatePlanOutput (near :331) validates definitionOfDone before verification: validate with the node's verification in hand so a text ref is checked against it. The frozen contract carries only indexes: normalize in toContractNode (src/plan/pipeline-shape.mjs near :86) or at the earliest point every frozen node passes, so validateContract never sees text.

Pin the test 'a plan proof names its verification by text or by index' in the new file test/plan/proof-ref.test.mjs: an index and an exact text both validate and freeze to the same index; a near miss is refused naming the node and its commands.
